title: AM-MultiModal-Monitoring: an integrated in-situ monitoring system for metal additive manufacturing with a detectability bound
description:
Code and documentation for a multi-modal in-situ monitoring system for laser powder-bed fusion and directed energy deposition, extended with a closed-form bound on what any detector could achieve given the sensing chain.

The system has two halves. A measurement chain classifies process state from acoustic emission, laser ultrasound, and phase / point-cloud data, using a unified Kalman fusion framework with offline edge intelligence. A decision layer states the ceiling of that chain: for a known signal in additive noise the matched filter maximises the deflection, so detection probability cannot exceed Phi(d' - z) whatever the model, and the geometry of the flaw enters through a single energy functional with two asymptotes. The decision layer is the twin detectability-bound package (v0.1.1, doi:10.5281/zenodo.24136698, concept 10.5281/zenodo.24080212), created in the same effort to answer the question the monitoring chain cannot — what could any detector see on it — and vendored here at that release (code identical to 81d99a2); the mapping between the two is in docs/TWIN_LIBRARIES.md.

Version 1.1.6 adds the reproducible per-subset cross-validation result (results/subset_cv.json, tools/compute_subset_cv.py) and retires the orphan cross-subset file. Version 1.1.5 corrects the clutter range quoted in the documentation: the measured values run from 23 to 125, not 24 to 125 (Table 6 has 23.3 at three voxels). Version 1.1.4 makes the four height-map paths literal stage inputs, so the readiness check sees them. Version 1.1.3 fixed the declared inputs of the height-map stage so the readiness check matches reality, and records a 12/12 end-to-end measured run on all six datasets. Version 1.1.2 recorded the twin relationship with the decision-layer package. Version 1.1.1 added the design-rule table and the hold-out metrics behind the acoustic row, and moved every statistics result from the gitignored data tree into results/. It also adds the real-data re-analyses behind the paper's acoustic spectral bound, fusion, laser-ultrasound echo detection, phase-unwrapping, white-light-interferometry, graded-decision and X-ray-CT clutter results, so that every measured table is reproduced by a registered stage, and the figure stage that draws the six manuscript figures from the result files. Provenance is a first-class property: a machine-generated registry of 36 analysis stages tags each one as measured (14), simulated (9) or derived (13), and the reporting layer refuses to merge the categories, so a simulated fusion result cannot be quoted as process evidence. The registry is produced from the source by a scanner and a test asserts that the two agree, so it cannot drift; a second test asserts that every dataset read by a measured stage is documented in the data guide.

Contents: the analysis scripts that produced the published figures, the real-data re-analyses, the figure stage, the orchestration package (registry, pipeline, decision layer, reporter, CLI), 20 tests, the detectability package, and the user guides in English and Chinese.
